O imparfait: como era antes: The imparfait: how things used to be
Formar o imparfait e usá-lo para hábitos: Form the imparfait and use it for past habits, descriptions and settings («quand j'étais petit, j'habitais à la campagne»).
PASSO 1: o imparfait descreve o passado: STEP 1: the imparfait describes a past that lasted, repeated or formed the setting. STEP 2: to form it, take the present-tense «nous» form and drop the «-ons»: «nous parlons → parl-», «nous finissons → finiss-», «nous prenons → pren-». STEP 3: add the endings: «-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient». So: «je parlais, tu parlais, il parlait, nous parlions, vous parliez, ils parlaient». STEP 4: the only irregular verb is «être»: stem «ét-»: «j'étais, tu étais, il était, nous étions, vous étiez, ils étaient». STEP 5: verbs in «-ger» and «-cer» keep the sound: «je mangeais, nous mangions» and «je commençais, nous commencions». STEP 6: «faire» → «je faisais» (from «nous faisons»); «avoir» → «j'avais»; «aller» → «j'allais». STEP 7: the endings «-ais, -ait, -aient» all sound the same: like the 'ay' in 'say'. The difference is only in the spelling. STEP 8: question and negation are the same as in the present: «Tu habitais où ?» «Je ne mangeais pas de viande.»
em português o pretérito imperfeito é «e: The English equivalent is «I used to speak» or «I was speaking». French is very similar in use («je parlais», «nous mangions»), and the form comes from the present-tense «nous» form, with no exception except «être».

PASSO 1: hábitos repetidos no passado: «: STEP 1: repeated habits in the past: «Quand j'étais petit, je jouais dans le jardin tous les jours.» STEP 2: descriptions of the past: «Ma grand-mère avait les cheveux blancs.» «La maison était grande.» STEP 3: the state of mind and the setting: «Il pleuvait, j'étais fatigué, je voulais rentrer.» STEP 4: age and time in the past: «J'avais dix ans.» «Il était huit heures.» STEP 5: words that go with it: «autrefois, avant, souvent, toujours, tous les jours, d'habitude, chaque été». STEP 6: «être en train de» in the past is the imparfait: «J'étais en train de manger.» STEP 7: with «si» for a suggestion: «Si on allait au cinéma ?» (what if we went to the cinema?). STEP 8: for nostalgia or a comparison between before and now: «Avant, il y avait moins de voitures.» «Maintenant, il y en a beaucoup.»
em português o imperfeito também descrev: In English, 'used to' and 'was … -ing' also describe and repeat («I used to play», «the house was big»). In French the use is very close; the thing to watch is not to swap it for «passé composé» when the action is a habit or a setting.

PASSO 1: use o imparfait para o antes e: STEP 1: use the imparfait for the 'before' and the present for the 'now': «Avant, j'habitais à la campagne. Maintenant, j'habite en ville.» STEP 2: connectors: «avant… maintenant», «autrefois… aujourd'hui», «à l'époque… maintenant». STEP 3: «ne… plus» marks what has ended: «Je ne joue plus au football.» «Il n'y a plus de ferme ici.» STEP 4: «toujours» or «encore» marks what continues: «J'habite toujours ici.» STEP 5: «avant» on its own opens a sentence about the past: «Avant, je prenais le bus.»
em português dizemos «antes eu morava aq: In English we say «I used to live here, now I live there». French does the same: «avant» + imparfait, «maintenant» + présent. The new ingredient is «ne… plus» («no longer / not any more»).
«Ne… plus» means «no longer / not any more».

Quando eu era pequeno, eu morava numa pe: When I was little, I lived in a small village with my grandparents. We had a big house with a garden. Every morning, I got up at seven o'clock and fed the chickens. In the afternoon, I played with my friends near the river. In summer, we swam almost every day. Now I live in the city and I no longer see my friends from the village, but I often think about that time.
